info.name: Cellphone Repair Shop API
info.description:
# Cellphone Repair Shop API

JSON API for a cellphone repair shop management system — repair intake and release, chain-of-custody proof, inventory across three item classes, point of sale, buy-back/refurb, and reporting. See `docs/design/01-domain-design.md` in the repo for the full domain design (ERDs, table catalogue, ticket state machine, error code catalogue).

This collection covers every endpoint implemented so far: health/readiness, auth, and the master-data contexts (branches, users, catalog, customers & devices). Later stages (repairs, chain of custody, inventory ledger, POS, buy-back, reporting) will extend this same collection as they ship — see the design doc §8 for the build order.

## Getting started

1. Make sure the API is running (`php artisan serve`) and `{{baseUrl}}` below matches it — defaults to `http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/v1`.
2. Run **Auth → Issue Token** first. It authenticates against a seeded demo user (`ricardo.santos@fixmo.test` / `password` — the owner; see `database/seeders/UserSeeder.php` for the full roster across both roles and branches) and automatically stores the bearer token in the `token` collection variable. Every other request in this collection inherits it via collection-level Bearer auth.
3. Every **Create** request in this collection captures the new record's `ulid` into a collection variable on success (e.g. creating a branch sets `branch_ulid`), so the Show/Update/Delete requests below it work immediately without manual copy-pasting.

## Conventions

- **Envelope.** Success responses are `{ "data": ..., "meta"?: ..., "links"?: ... }`. Errors are always `{ "error": { "code", "message", "details" } }` — clients switch on `code`, never on `message` text.
- **IDs are ULIDs, not sequential ids.** Every path parameter *and every foreign-key field in a request body* (`branch_ulid`, `device_brand_ulid`, `product_category_ulid`, `compatible_device_model_ulids`, ...) is a ULID. The API never exposes the internal `BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT` id anywhere a client can see it.
- **Idempotency-Key.** Every write request here sends a fresh `{{$guid}}` as `Idempotency-Key`. Resending the exact same key with the exact same body returns the original cached response; the same key with a *different* body returns `409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT`. Try it: send a Create request twice with "Send" — Postman regenerates `{{$guid}}` each time by design, so to see the replay behavior, copy the header value from one request into the next send manually.
- **Pagination & filtering.** List endpoints return page pagination (`meta.current_page`, `meta.total`, etc.) and accept `filter[field]=value`, `sort=field` / `sort=-field` (descending), and `page=`. Each List request below has the allow-listed filter/sort query params present but disabled — enable the ones you want.
- **Permissions.** Endpoints are gated by the permissions seeded in `RoleAndPermissionSeeder` (e.g. `branches.manage`, `catalog.manage`, `reports.margin.view`). The seeded owner (`ricardo.santos@fixmo.test`) has every permission; try authenticating as a cashier or technician (see the seeder for emails, same `password`) to see `403 FORBIDDEN` and permission-gated fields (e.g. a product's `cost` field disappears entirely for a cashier) in action.

## Error code catalogue (implemented so far)

| HTTP | code | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 401 | `UNAUTHENTICATED` | Missing/invalid/expired bearer token |
| 403 | `FORBIDDEN` | Authenticated but lacks the permission |
| 404 | `NOT_FOUND` | ULID doesn't resolve, or resolves outside your branch scope |
| 405 | `METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED` | Verb not supported on the route |
| 409 | `IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT` | Same `Idempotency-Key` replayed with a different body |
| 422 | `VALIDATION_FAILED` | Form Request failure; see `error.details[]` per field |
| 429 | `RATE_LIMITED` | Limiter exceeded |
| 500 | `INTERNAL_ERROR` | Unhandled throwable — still JSON, never HTML |
| 503 | `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` | `/ready` dependency (DB/Redis/queue) is down |

The full catalogue, including business codes for stages not yet built (`IMEI_MISMATCH`, `UNIT_ALREADY_SOLD`, `SHIFT_NOT_OPEN`, ...), is in `docs/design/01-domain-design.md` §5.

request.description: Issues a Sanctum bearer token. Every other request in this collection uses the `token` collection variable this sets automatically.

item.name: Branches
item.description: No destroy endpoint — closing a branch is `is_active = false` via Update, not a row removal (see design doc Flag 1). Requires `branches.manage` to create/update, `branches.view` to read (every seeded role has view).

item.name: Find My Branch (used by Users/Customers below)

request.description: Looks up the seeded owner's own branch (Quezon City, the demo user in Auth > Issue Token belongs here) and stores it as owner_branch_ulid. Deliberately NOT the branch created below — BranchScope hides records in a different branch than the authenticated user's own, even for an owner, so Create User/Create Customer need this branch, not a freshly created one, for the Show/Update requests underneath them to find anything.

item.name: Users
item.description: Requires `users.manage` to create/update/delete, `users.view` to read (owner + manager only in the seeded permission set).

request.description: role must be one of owner, manager, cashier, technician. Uses owner_branch_ulid (run Branches > Find My Branch first) rather than a freshly created branch — see that request's description for why.

item.name: Catalog
item.description: Requires `catalog.manage` to create/update/delete, `catalog.view` to read (every seeded role has view).

request.description: filter[device_brand_id] takes the brand's internal id, not its ulid, per spatie/laravel-query-builder's exact-match filter — a known asymmetry versus request-body fields, noted for whoever builds an SDK against this.
Run Device Brands > Create Device Brand first so device_brand_ulid is set.

`cost` only appears in the response for a user with `reports.margin.view` (the seeded owner/manager) — a cashier sees `selling_price` but not `cost`. category and brand are always eager-loaded; compatibleDeviceModels is opt-in via `include=`.
type is one of handset, accessory, part. Run Product Categories > Create and Device Brands > Create first so the ulid variables are set.

item.name: Customers
item.description: Requires `customers.manage` to create/update/delete, `customers.view` to read (every seeded role has view). mobile accepts common PH formats (09XXXXXXXXX, +639XXXXXXXXX, spaces/dashes) and is normalized to +63XXXXXXXXXX before storing.

body.raw:
{
  "branch_ulid": "{{owner_branch_ulid}}",
  "name": "Juan Dela Cruz",
  "mobile": "0917 123 4567",
  "email": "juan.delacruz@example.com",
  "address": "123 Mabini St., Quezon City",
  "notes": "Prefers SMS updates.",
  "is_blacklisted": false
}

request.description: Uses owner_branch_ulid (see Branches > Find My Branch) so the authenticated owner's BranchScope can actually see this record in the Show/Update requests below.

item.name: Customer Devices
item.description: Nested under a customer. imei accepts raw digits or common separators, is normalized, and validated as 15 digits passing the Luhn checksum (App\Rules\ValidImei). Same customers.view/customers.manage permissions as Customers.

request.description: The default {{imei}} (490154203237518) is a well-known valid Luhn-checksum test IMEI. Run Customers > Create Customer and Catalog > Device Models > Create first.
404s if customer_device_ulid doesn't belong to customer_ulid — devices are checked against their parent customer, not just looked up globally.

Returns every customer_devices row for this IMEI across every customer — and every branch — that ever brought it in, not scoped to one customer or one branch. This is the differentiator described in docs/design/01-domain-design.md §2.3: a repeat repair is recognized even if the customer's first visit was at a different branch.

item.name: Cleanup (run last)
item.description: Every destructive request from the folders above, in reverse dependency order, plus revoking the token this run's Auth → Issue Token created. Deliberately kept out of the main top-to-bottom flow — running these mid-collection would delete/soft-delete records (Customers, Users, and every Catalog model are soft-deletable) that later folders still depend on via the ulid variables captured above; a soft-deleted record 404s on every subsequent lookup because of BranchScope/the default Eloquent soft-delete scope. Run this folder by itself once you're done exploring, or just leave it — it's harmless to skip since re-running the collection from the top always creates fresh records.

request.description: The one hard delete in this folder — CustomerDevice isn't soft-deletable.
A user can't delete themself — UserPolicy::delete blocks it (403). This is a different user than the one issuing the token, so it should succeed.

tokenId is the numeric id from Auth > List My Tokens (this is the one route that isn't ULID-keyed — Sanctum's own token model). Defaults to 1, which — in a single fresh run of this collection — is the same token Logout below revokes too; running both is redundant but harmless (the second is a no-op 401/404 against an already-gone token). Issue a second token first if you want to see this revoke a token you're not currently using.
Run this absolutely last — every request above needs the token this invalidates.
